title: On Scaring the birds from the field
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：scare　|　正文 354 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 scare 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the craftsman ① scared the birds from the field with great care, and every apprentice in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the craftsman ② scares the birds from the field on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ scare the birds from the field at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ scared the birds from the field before — a line in the ledger for August 1960 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Scaring the birds from the field with great care, the craftsman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ scare everybody half out of their wits on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Scare everybody half out of their wits at once and never mention it again.

By 1973 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the ledger, and a new apprentice from the next workshop ⑧ scares everybody half out of their wits with great care every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ scared the birds from the field again when nobody else would.

⑩ To scare the birds from the field, my mother said in 1978, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody scares the birds from the field on the same day again and somebody must scare the birds from the field with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 惊吓（一般过去式 scared the birds from the field：1966 年匠人头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 惊吓（一般现在 scares the birds from the field：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 惊吓（不定式 to scare the birds from the field：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 惊吓（过去完成时 had scared the birds from the field：1960 年八月的工料簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 惊吓（动名词 scaring the birds from the field 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 吓走（scare everybody half out of their wits：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去吓走把大家吓得半死）
G. v. 吓走（scare everybody half out of their wits：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 惊吓（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 scares everybody half out of their wits，而母亲又一次 scared the birds from the field）

answers.why: scare 意为“惊吓”，1966 年匠人小心翼翼地惊吓把鸟从地里吓走，那是工坊里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 scared。
scare 意为“惊吓”，自那以后匠人当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 scares。
scare 意为“惊吓”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯惊吓把鸟从地里吓走”，此处为不定式 to scare the birds from the field。
scare 意为“惊吓”，工料簿里 八月 那行字说明早在 1973 年之前就有人惊吓过，故用过去完成时 had scared。
scare 意为“惊吓”，匠人说“惊吓把鸟从地里吓走这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 scaring the birds from the field 作主语。
scare 意为“吓走”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去吓走把大家吓得半死”，should ever 之后用原形 scare everybody half out of their wits。
scare 意为“吓走”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻吓走把大家吓得半死（scare everybody half out of their wits at once），以后再也不要提起。
scare 意为“惊吓”，新来的学徒每个年头都照例吓走把大家吓得半死，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 scares。
scare 意为“惊吓”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地惊吓把鸟从地里吓走，用一般过去式 scared 叙述。
scare 意为“惊吓”，结尾那句是母亲 1978 年的话：要惊吓把鸟从地里吓走，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工坊记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 scare 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1966 the craftsman scared the birds from the field with great care, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the craftsman scares the birds from the field on the same day whenever the workshop asks.
Scaring the birds from the field with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever scare everybody half out of their wits on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next workshop scares everybody half out of their wits with great care every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother scared the birds from the field again, and the workshop remembered that half.
